findings.title: Selecting a remote part of an accepted POI footprint opens another source hex rather than that POI's content
repro: Import regionFixture() as v11 with map.seas=[], map.nextSeaId=1 and classification.discoveryByPoi['poi:1:2,0']={mode:'interaction',clueText:'OWNER-ONE-CLUE'}.
Enable edit; editDetailFootprintExtent(detail-poi:1, manual conditional provenance, cells q=12 through18,r=0). This is a valid connected footprint crossing accepted dry geography.
Exit edit, setDetailViewStep(1), selectDetailCell({q:12,r:0}), then selectDetailCell({q:18,r:0}).
findings.expected: Each occupied part resolves the same POI entity and makes its accepted clue/content/actions available; multiple owners need an owner selection action. Terrain location may stay distinct from the selected entity.
findings.actual: Both summaries correctly contain detail-poi:1 / poi:1:2,0, but selectedHex changes from2,0 to3,0. The real knavePanel contains OWNER-ONE-CLUE at12,0 and has no POI text at18,0. Summary rows show geometry/provenance/attachments, with no owner-content selection. 'Show detail' chooses cells[0] and still routes through coordinate selection; ordering/manual shapes cannot establish owner identity.
findings.impact: Valid explicit cross-source extents and overlapping POIs can show the correct POI name in the summary while its source content/editor context is absent or belongs to a different location. Saved entity/content remains intact; this is selection/context failure, not demonstrated payload loss.
findings.suggested_boundary: Keep entity selection keyed by poiId/legacyRef separately from the clicked geographical source cell; expose selection from every summary owner and resolve source-specific content/editor actions through that identity.

findings.title: Active v11 layer with live POI owners accepts deletion of all footprints
repro: Export the valid active one-POI map from agent-work/evidence/review-HX-BL-051-a4e8a48/hx-review-repro.mjs.
Set only map.physicalGrid.poiFootprints=[]; retain active=true and the existing poiIdentities/live POI.
findings.expected: An active DETAIL1 document must cover every live owner. Reject missing coverage before map/history writes; legacy documents with no physicalGrid remain separately supported. If an intermediate identity-only checkpoint is supported, distinguish it as unadapted rather than treating it as an active displayed layer.
findings.actual: Import reports no alert, commits one transaction and accepts active=true with one live identity and zero footprints. Summary now reports zero POIs; active map renderer suppresses legacy markers and renders only footprints, so the POI disappears from the map layer. Exact Undo restores the accepted document; no claim that source POI text is erased.
findings.cause: validateDetail1Document invokes the full live spatial/coverage validator only when poiFootprints.length>0. An empty array bypasses the very incomplete_footprint_coverage check that rejects a partially missing layer.
findings.compatibility_note: Existing saveSafety and regionEditing tests intentionally accept identity-only checkpoints; this explains the hole but does not satisfy the approved active full-coverage contract. Fix should preserve legitimate legacy/unadapted states through an explicit state boundary and update those tests accordingly.

test_quality.assessment: The geometry/identity/placement/parser/controller tests cover distinct meaningful risks: precise intersections and topology, capital/Seat defaults, water/route source identity, atomic stale/invalid failures, edit/remap/delete/history/import compatibility. They do more than count successful calls and use real App harness callbacks for state operations. Existing fixtures are extended, so no finding of gratuitous duplication is justified.
test_quality.limits: Pure summaries and callback tests do not establish real pointer/keyboard/touch owner-content selection. The new browser workflow uses one capital; overview loops assert DOM target presence and screenshots later return to1mile. Its green status cannot close DTL26 gaps. Changing crafted generation fixtures to delete stale physicalGrid is reasonable when testing legacy/import contracts, but it excludes active footprint integration there; separate detailGeography tests supply narrower active coverage. Identity-only fixture additions are weaker than full footprints and explicitly explain accepted empty-state behavior. The reproduced identity-context defect is not detected by existing single-cell and summary-ID assertions. Identity-only active checkpoint tests also encode the incomplete active-layer acceptance hole; they need adjustment to preserve legacy compatibility without bypassing full active footprint coverage.
test_quality.source_fixture_caveat: riverBackendFixture changes setup across existing E5 tests; no automatic counting of helper users as newly added cases.
